# Durable scheduled release publishing

Original scope: SPEC invariant 8 requires releases and scheduled publishing. The
previous release implementation only stored `publishAt`; no host operation ever
executed due releases. This checkpoint adds explicit trusted host execution,
shared manual/scheduled claims, durable per-document intents/results, schema-2
migration/backfill and actual Studio scheduling/outcome controls.

## Runtime contract

- `server.executeDueReleases()` and the exported host function scan a bounded due
  index. Future times survive restart. No timer or provider call starts at import
  or construction. The host owns cadence, monitored invocation and graceful drain.
- Manual and due paths use the same sorted membership snapshot and monotonic
  version CAS. Lease expiry permits takeover; only a successful competing version
  update supersedes the prior owner. Post-I/O writes cannot overwrite a winner.
- Persist exact workflow-checked revision, type, stable key and subject before
  sending. ContentFn's actor-bound durable replay resolves a committed publish
  whose response was lost, including after draft removal and database reopen.
- Current service permissions and, for manual calls, requesting-user permissions
  are checked. Unknown datasets, role failures and workflow/revision conflicts
  fail closed. Known per-document failures continue deterministically. Transient
  prerequisites retain due work; unknown publication remains `uncertain`.
- A changed subject, unavailable replay contract or unknown legacy manual send
  cannot become a fresh publication. No automatic key changes or blind retries.
- The due query selects identifiers/version only, not every candidate's document
  payload. Storage uses the existing shared adapter/schema wrapper. Both journal
  and membership reads/writes detach native JSON references so callers cannot
  bypass CAS by mutating returned objects.
- Studio creates optional UTC schedules through actual authorized endpoints and
  displays durable completion/failure/pending outcomes. It never equates an
  uncertain or partial batch with completion.

Producer prerequisite: ordinary merge of ContentFn
`ea74ce3a84e662353dd8eaff3ae0676fa2127548` (sf-next PR 56). Its precise
`content.docs.publish.idempotency.v1` contract binds dataset/key/input/actor and
requires a verified nonempty subject. Legacy successful anonymous keys retain the
same record identity and deterministically conflict under the stronger contract.

## Verification

Commands use the CMS checkout's Node 20.20.0 and its matching native SQLite ABI:

- `npm test -w ./cmsfn/server`: 123 passed across 20 files, before the additional
  legacy-uncertainty assertion; subsequent scheduler run passed all 12 tests.
- `npm test -w ./cmsfn/studio`: 84 passed across 18 files.
- Focused scheduler/concurrent-release/SQLite-storage checks after native JSON
  detachment: 18 passed; the later added legacy case also passed.
- `npm run typecheck -w ./cmsfn/server` and `npm run typecheck -w ./cmsfn/studio`:
  passed. `npx --yes turbo@2.6.1 run build --filter=@cmsfn/studio...
  --filter=@cmsfn/server...`: 31 tasks passed.
- Native SQLite evidence includes exact due boundary, reopen, two independent
  simultaneous claimers, stale post-I/O owner fencing, manual overlap, lost ACK
  after producer commit, termination before send, revision retention, bounded
  batch continuation, policy outage/denial, changed subject, old-table additive
  DDL/backfill, invalid legacy dates and detached memory state.
- `python3 cmsfn/.conduct/studio-packed-acceptance.py --producer-root
  /Volumes/Dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/contentfn-sf-next-readiness`: normal npm
  11 clean packed installation, production-only audit, full native Chromium
  143.0.7499.4 App with actual CMS/Content HTTP endpoints, strict installed JSX/CJS
  consumers and ESM/CJS SSR exports. Browser execution performs 154 HTTP requests,
  creates a schedule, loses the response after real ContentFn publication commits,
  shows uncertainty, recovers the original key and proves exactly one publish
  audit entry. No fake replacement producer endpoint or copied Studio subset.

The initial CMS native run under Node 22 encountered the checkout's existing
Node-20-only SQLite binary; final CMS native checks use matching Node 20.20.0.
One intermediate full run saw an unrelated roles HTTP response containing `old`;
the same unmodified test passed in the subsequent full suite. The final native
scheduler/storage checks remain independent of that mocked role fixture.

## Deployment and remaining boundaries

See `cmsfn/server/README.md` for exact schema-2 DDL, bounded idempotent backfill,
invalid-row reporting and host configuration. Drain old writers before migration;
`releaseExecutionSchemaVersion: 2` is a host assertion, not distributed old-binary
fencing. Existing SQL tables must migrate before this version's release writes.
Retain producer replay records and stable identity until unresolved runs settle;
dataset deletion/recreation or database rollback is outside replay guarantees.

Publication is deterministic per-document best effort, not dataset-atomic. The
latest terminal journal is retained until an explicit new manual run replaces it;
producer audit is the archival record. Unresolved runs are not automatically
expired. Custom storage-adapter deadlines and host callback cancellation remain
host responsibilities. This slice did not deploy a worker, migrate production,
exercise external SQL services, send provider webhooks, or validate native Safari.
History and remaining original Studio operational acceptance remain open; this is
not a declaration that all CMS readiness requirements are complete.

  prerequisites retain due work; unknown publication remains `uncertain`.
- A changed subject, unavailable replay contract or unknown legacy manual send
  cannot become a fresh publication. No automatic key changes or blind retries.
- The due query selects identifiers/version only, not every candidate's document
  payload. Storage uses the existing shared adapter/schema wrapper. Both journal
  and membership reads/writes detach native JSON references so callers cannot
  bypass CAS by mutating returned objects.
- Studio creates optional UTC schedules through actual authorized endpoints and
  displays durable completion/failure/pending outcomes. It never equates an
  uncertain or partial batch with completion.

Producer prerequisite: ordinary merge of ContentFn
`ea74ce3a84e662353dd8eaff3ae0676fa2127548` (sf-next PR 56). Its precise
`content.docs.publish.idempotency.v1` contract binds dataset/key/input/actor and
requires a verified nonempty subject. Legacy successful anonymous keys retain the
same record identity and deterministically conflict under the stronger contract.

## Verification

Commands use the CMS checkout's Node 20.20.0 and its matching native SQLite ABI:

- `npm test -w ./cmsfn/server`: 123 passed across 20 files, before the additional
  legacy-uncertainty assertion; subsequent scheduler run passed all 12 tests.
- `npm test -w ./cmsfn/studio`: 84 passed across 18 files.
- Focused scheduler/concurrent-release/SQLite-storage checks after native JSON
  detachment: 18 passed; the later added legacy case also passed.
- `npm run typecheck -w ./cmsfn/server` and `npm run typecheck -w ./cmsfn/studio`:
  passed. `npx --yes turbo@2.6.1 run build --filter=@cmsfn/studio...
  --filter=@cmsfn/server...`: 31 tasks passed.
- Native SQLite evidence includes exact due boundary, reopen, two independent
  simultaneous claimers, stale post-I/O owner fencing, manual overlap, lost ACK
  after producer commit, termination before send, revision retention, bounded
  batch continuation, policy outage/denial, changed subject, old-table additive
  DDL/backfill, invalid legacy dates and detached memory state.
- `python3 cmsfn/.conduct/studio-packed-acceptance.py --producer-root
  /Volumes/Dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/contentfn-sf-next-readiness`: normal npm
  11 clean packed installation, production-only audit, full native Chromium
  143.0.7499.4 App with actual CMS/Content HTTP endpoints, strict installed JSX/CJS
  consumers and ESM/CJS SSR exports. Browser execution performs 154 HTTP requests,
  creates a schedule, loses the response after real ContentFn publication commits,
  shows uncertainty, recovers the original key and proves exactly one publish
  audit entry. No fake replacement producer endpoint or copied Studio subset.

The initial CMS native run under Node 22 encountered the checkout's existing
Node-20-only SQLite binary; final CMS native checks use matching Node 20.20.0.
One intermediate full run saw an unrelated roles HTTP response containing `old`;
the same unmodified test passed in the subsequent full suite. The final native
scheduler/storage checks remain independent of that mocked role fixture.

## Deployment and remaining boundaries

See `cmsfn/server/README.md` for exact schema-2 DDL, bounded idempotent backfill,
invalid-row reporting and host configuration. Drain old writers before migration;
`releaseExecutionSchemaVersion: 2` is a host assertion, not distributed old-binary
fencing. Existing SQL tables must migrate before this version's release writes.
Retain producer replay records and stable identity until unresolved runs settle;
dataset deletion/recreation or database rollback is outside replay guarantees.

Publication is deterministic per-document best effort, not dataset-atomic. The
latest terminal journal is retained until an explicit new manual run replaces it;
producer audit is the archival record. Unresolved runs are not automatically
expired. Custom storage-adapter deadlines and host callback cancellation remain
host responsibilities. This slice did not deploy a worker, migrate production,
exercise external SQL services, send provider webhooks, or validate native Safari.
History and remaining original Studio operational acceptance remain open; this is

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── README.md
```

### Examples

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`
- `cachefn/typescript/` + `cachefn/python/`
- `secfn/typescript/` + `secfn/python/`
- `plugfn/core/` + `plugfn/python/`
- `drawfn/core/` (TypeScript only, with React/Svelte adapters)
- `searchfn/` (TypeScript only, browser-focused)

## 🔧 Development Workflow

### Building

```bash
# Build all packages
npm run build

# Build specific package (from root)
turbo run build --filter=authfn
turbo run build --filter=@superfunctions/db

# Build from package directory
cd authfn/ts-sdk && npm run build
```

### Testing

```bash
# Test all packages
npm test

# Test specific package
turbo run test --filter=drawfn

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch
```

### Linting

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Package Manager

- **npm** (v10.2.0+) - Specified in `packageManager` field
- Uses npm workspaces for monorepo management
- Turbo for build orchestration

## 🎯 Key Superfunctions Features

### AuthFn

- Multi-provider authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT)
- Framework-agnostic with adapters for Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- Database-agnostic (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- TypeScript + Python SDKs

### DrawFn

- Cross-framework drawing canvas
- React and Svelte adapters
- Scene management, export capabilities
- Tolerant parsing with version validation

### PlugFn

- Self-hosted integration platform
- 75+ provider integrations (GitHub, Slack, Discord, Linear, Stripe)
- OAuth 2.0 flow handling
- Webhook support
- Multi-tenant with secure token storage

### SearchFn

- Browser-first full-text search
- IndexedDB persistence with in-memory LRU cache
- BM25 scoring
- FlexSearch-compatible API
- Worker-ready with snapshot export/import

### MailFn

- Stable and expiring programmable inboxes
- Cloudflare Email Workers, D1, R2, and Queues deployment adapter
- Raw MIME and attachment evidence, waits, OTP/link extraction, threads, labels, and search
- Typed client, test helpers, CLI, MCP server, custom domains, webhooks, and SendFn composition
- Scoped credentials, retention, audit, quotas, and explicitly gated public-platform controls

### CacheFn

- Multi-tier caching (memory, IndexedDB, external)
- Function memoization
- TTL and invalidation strategies
- Browser and server support

### SecFn

- Secrets vault management
- Access control and permissions
- Rate limiting
- Security monitoring
- Secret scanning

### BotFn

- Multi-platform bot framework
- Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations
- Shared types and persistence layer
- Event-driven architecture

## 🛠️ Common Tasks

### Adding a New Function

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`
4. Create `.conduct/` for artifacts
5. Add to workspace in root `package.json`
6. Package name: `{functionname}` (not scoped unless multi-package)

### Adding a Shared Package

1. Create in `packages/{name}/`
2. Package name: `@superfunctions/{name}`
3. Add to workspace (already covered by `packages/*`)
4. Update dependent packages

### Creating Artifacts

1. Function-specific: `{function}/.conduct/{artifact}.md`
2. Shared/root: `_conduct/{artifact}.md`
3. Use consistent naming: `implementation.md`, `spec.md`, `audit_report.md`, etc.

### Working with Turbo

```bash
# Run task across all packages
turbo run build
turbo run test

# Run for specific package
turbo run build --filter=authfn

# Run with dependencies
turbo run build --filter=authfn...

# Clear cache
turbo run clean
```

## 📚 Important Files

### Root Configuration

- `package.json` - Workspace and script definitions
- `turbo.json` - Turbo build configuration
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript base config (if exists)

### Package Configuration

- `package.json` - Package metadata, dependencies, scripts
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript configuration
- `vitest.config.ts` - Test configuration
- `pyproject.toml` - Python package configuration

### Documentation

- `README.md` - Package overview and usage
- `SPEC.md` - Technical specification (common in larger functions)
- `.conduct/*.md` - Implementation plans, audits, tasks

## 🔍 Finding Code

### Search Patterns

- **Function implementations**: `{function}/typescript/src/` or `{function}/python/{function}/`
- **Tests**: `__tests__/`, `tests/`, `*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`
- **Types**: `types.ts`, `models.py`, `src/types/`

export async function listHistory(
  config: RevisionsStorageConfig,
  input: {
    dataset: string;
    id: string;
    limit?: number;
    cursor?: string | null;
  }

  ContentfnEnvelope<{
    revisions: ContentfnDocument[];
    nextCursor: string | null;

/**

 * Returns revisions ordered by timestamp DESC, then rev ASC as tie-breaker.

export async function listHistory(
  config: RevisionsStorageConfig,
  input: {
    dataset: string;
    id: string;
    limit?: number;
    cursor?: string | null;
  }
): Promise<
  ContentfnEnvelope<{
    revisions: ContentfnDocument[];
    nextCursor: string | null;
  }>
> {
  if (!await datasetExists(config, input.dataset)) return err("DATASET_NOT_FOUND", "Dataset not found", { dataset: input.dataset });

  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(limit) || limit < 1 || limit > 1000) return err("VALIDATION_FAILED", "History limit must be an integer from 1 to 1000", { path: "limit" });
  const docId = input.id.startsWith("drafts.") ? input.id.substring(7) : input.id;

  const where = [
    { field: "dataset", operator: "eq" as const, value: input.dataset },
  ];

  const revisions = await config.db.findMany({
    model: CONTENTFN_TABLE_NAMES.revisions,
    where,
  });

  const filtered = revisions.filter(
    (r: any) => r.docId === docId || r.docId === `drafts.${docId}`

  filtered.sort((a: any, b: any) => {
    const tsCompare = b.timestamp.localeCompare(a.timestamp);
    if (tsCompare !== 0) return tsCompare;
    return a.rev < b.rev ? -1 : a.rev > b.rev ? 1 : 0;

      return err("VALIDATION_FAILED", "Invalid cursor", { path: "cursor" });
    }

    page.length === limit && startIdx + limit < filtered.length

            rev: (page[page.length - 1] as any).rev,

# Document history pagination prerequisite

CMS DESK-001/TV-DESK-PANES-001 requires the real ContentFn `docs.history`
revision list, newest first, with denied readers receiving no revision content.
The existing producer returned full snapshots but loaded every dataset revision.

History now scopes every revision query by dataset and both base/draft document
identities. The total order is timestamp DESC, revision ASC, storage identity ASC.
The shared flat-predicate adapter uses three disjoint keyset ranges with at most
`limit + 1` rows each; merged pages return at most the requested limit. Version-1
cursors bind dataset/base document; legacy unbound cursors require first-page

ContentFn `/contentfn/docs/history` endpoint and displays full immutable draft

parsing; oversized or malformed pages fail visibly rather than show partial data.

proxy/session integration for the ContentFn API.

Old timestamp/revision-only cursors now fail validation: restart from the\nfirst page after upgrading.', 'Version-2 opaque cursors bind a compact hash of that scope; `drafts.id` and `id`\naddress the same history, including unrestricted long public IDs. Safely parseable\nversion-1 dataset/document-bound cursors remain accepted. Old unbound\ntimestamp/revision-only cursors fail validation: restart from the first page.',1);start=s.index('Each page materializes at most');s=s[:start]+'''Each page materializes at most `6 * (limit + 1)` candidate rows using disjoint
keyset ranges for each exact base/draft identity. First pages use two queries;
continuations use six. The host must install the directional index below to avoid
scanning/sorting an entire document history. These are shared-adapter reads, not
an additional SQL runtime.

### Install the ordered history index

Existing and fresh databases can call `upgradeHistoryIndexSchema` after table
creation. It passes `getHistoryIndexDefinition()` to the host's idempotent
`ensureOrderedIndex` implementation:

```ts
import { upgradeHistoryIndexSchema } from "@contentfn/server";
await upgradeHistoryIndexSchema({
  async ensureOrderedIndex(index) {
    // Inspect existing indexes using the host's schema tools. If the same name
    // exists, verify fields, directions and uniqueness; reject a mismatch.
    // Otherwise create the following nonunique index in the normal DDL path.
  },
});
```

Required definition (SQLite syntax):

```sql
CREATE INDEX contentfn_revisions_history_v1
ON contentfn_revisions (dataset ASC, docId ASC, timestamp DESC, rev ASC, id ASC);
```

Do not treat `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` alone as verification: a same-name
index with different columns/directions must fail readiness. Index creation is
additive and requires no row backfill; failures leave the previous data readable.
The hook is explicit and never runs at import/server construction. Deployments
choose maintenance/online-DDL policy appropriate to their database.

The shared `IndexSchema`/schema CLI currently cannot express mixed directions,
so this descriptor is separate and the CLI does not establish ordered-index
readiness. Keep this index in the host migration inventory. SQLite native tests
verify populated first/deep page plans use indexed range searches without a
temporary sort. PostgreSQL/MySQL execution plans and online migrations have not
been validated here. In particular, unrestricted public `docId` values are TEXT;
MySQL prefix indexes/byte budgets and PostgreSQL index-entry limits need a distinct
bounded-key design before claiming equivalent performance for all supported IDs.
Memory storage keeps functional behavior but has no physical index acceleration.
''';p.write_text(s)
PY

# Ordered history index and long-identity cursors

The prior history checkpoint bounded materialized rows but left database scan/sort
cost open. This checkpoint splits base/draft identities into exact shared-adapter
queries and supplies an explicit ordered-index migration descriptor/hook. First
pages perform two index seeks; continuation pages perform three disjoint ranges
per identity, at most six seeks and `6 * (limit + 1)` materialized candidates.
Total ordering and full snapshot/authorization contracts remain unchanged.

`getHistoryIndexDefinition()` supplies nonunique
`contentfn_revisions_history_v1(dataset ASC, docId ASC, timestamp DESC, rev ASC,
id ASC)`. `upgradeHistoryIndexSchema(hostAdapter)` invokes the host's normal
schema migration implementation. The host must verify existing same-name indexes
including directions and uniqueness, and reject a mismatch. It runs explicitly
on fresh/existing tables; no automatic DDL or parallel SQL query runtime is added.
The shared schema CLI cannot currently represent directions, so it does not
establish this migration's readiness. See server README for the actual DDL and
host contract.

New version-2 cursors bind the existing SHA-256 documentStorageId scope instead
of embedding unrestricted public IDs. This fixes valid long IDs producing their
own oversized/unusable cursor. Safe version-1 scoped cursors remain accepted;
unbound legacy cursors still reject. Cross-document/dataset denial remains.

Validation with Node 22.22.0:

- Focused history/index/keyset: 9 passed; strict server types passed.
- Full server: 210 passed, 2 external SQL tests skipped (32 passing files).
- Turbo ContentFn dependency build: 13 tasks passed.
- Normal npm 11 clean production packed install: zero audit vulnerabilities;
  installed real HTTP revision pages, long-ID paging, bound cursor denial,
  permission denial and exported migration failure propagation passed.
- Native SQLite populates 50,000 rows (40,000 unrelated and 10,000 requested
  history rows, with equal timestamps/revisions across draft/published versions).
  Repeated migration preserves all rows; incompatible same-name index rejects.
  First/next/deep pages return the expected mixed-direction/tie order. All 14
  actual generated SELECT query plans use the ordered index, with neither SCAN
  nor TEMP B-TREE:

```text
SEARCH contentfn_revisions USING INDEX contentfn_revisions_history_v1 (dataset=? AND docId=?)
SEARCH contentfn_revisions USING INDEX contentfn_revisions_history_v1 (dataset=? AND docId=? AND timestamp<?)
SEARCH contentfn_revisions USING INDEX contentfn_revisions_history_v1 (dataset=? AND docId=? AND timestamp=? AND rev>?)
SEARCH contentfn_revisions USING INDEX contentfn_revisions_history_v1 (dataset=? AND docId=? AND timestamp=? AND rev=? AND id>?)
```

Receipts: `/tmp/content-history-index-{focused,types,full,build,packed}.log`.

This is actual populated SQLite plan evidence, not a universal provider claim.
PostgreSQL/MySQL plans/online migration remain unverified. Unrestricted TEXT
public IDs also require a separate bounded-key index design before PostgreSQL
entry-size/MySQL byte-prefix constraints can preserve the same performance
contract for all IDs. Memory storage has functional behavior without physical
index acceleration. No live database migration, provider send or deployment.
EOF

# Studio import/export and authorization checkpoint

## Original requirement and chosen scope

OPS-001 is P0: authorized import/export with dataset isolation; its acceptance explicitly says cross-dataset import attempts are denied or fail deterministically. ContentFn separately supports environment promotion and explicitly documents importing an archive into another target dataset. CMS therefore now defaults to same-dataset restores. A trusted server `authorizeCrossDatasetImport(req, { sourceDataset, targetDataset })` callback may explicitly authorize a migration after target `audit.read` and configured-dataset checks. Missing, false or throwing policy denies it. Artifact source metadata is untrusted provenance; the separately authorized request dataset remains the write target. This preserves the default CMS requirement without removing ContentFn's intentional migration capability.

## Behavior

The existing routes allowed missing role configuration and used an unbounded parser. Real HTTP baseline tests reproduced anonymous export/import and implicit cross-dataset import. Both routes now fail closed on missing, denied or failed identity resolution. They reuse the shared bounded JSON parser: 64 KiB export request and 25 MiB import request. Structural archive checks precede forwarding; actual ContentFn remains authoritative for deep schema/document validation and atomic import. Explicit server-owned `contentfnOpsHeaders` resolves only after local authorization, without implicitly copying browser credentials. Callback failures are sanitized.

Upstream export responses are bounded to 25 MiB and import responses to 64 KiB, with a 30-second timeout and redirects rejected. An import timeout does not establish rollback. The UI reports uncertain import outcomes and does not automatically retry. Oversized archives fail instead of being truncated; larger archive streaming/job support is not established here.

The complete App now exposes Import / export for the configured selected dataset. Export provides the entire compact JSON archive as a download and read-only text, replacing the previous 500-character truncation. Import shows an explicit target, overwrite semantics, success or error. Pending operations cannot double-submit. Dataset changes clear old archives/results and ignore prior completions. Blob URLs are revoked when replaced or unmounted. No browser configuration contains upstream service credentials.

## Evidence

- Baseline HTTP regressions: `/tmp/cms-ops-before.log` reproduces both missing-identity forwarding and default migration success before correction.
- `npm test -w ./cmsfn/server`: 107 tests/18 files passed. New HTTP cases cover missing/throwing/denied identity, default migration denial, explicit migration callback, target permission precedence, sanitized callback errors, malformed bodies/artifacts and oversized export/import requests without producer calls.
- `npm test -w ./cmsfn/studio`: 82 tests/18 files passed, including complete artifact/download, success, scoped late export, malformed JSON no request and import uncertainty without duplicate submissions.
- Server and Studio `npm run typecheck` passed. Turbo Studio/server dependency build: 31 tasks successful, 29 cached; both changed packages rebuilt with declarations.
- `python3 cmsfn/.conduct/studio-packed-acceptance.py --producer-root /Volumes/Dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/contentfn-sf-next-readiness` passed with real ContentFn `fdd2678a244c208a713e3df729f5907fcca960d1`. The complete installed App ran in Chromium 143.0.7499.4 with 118 actual API requests, retaining earlier authoring, singleton, audit and release checks. New acceptance downloaded a complete archive, changed then restored a document, rejected duplicate malformed snapshots without mutation, denied migration by default, enabled only explicit prod-to-staging migration, checked both source and target values, and denied operations after role revocation. The real producer required the trusted server header for HTTP import/export.
- Fresh normal npm 11 packed production install: 174 packages audited, zero advisories; adding consumer tooling: 185 packages, zero advisories. Strict installed NodeNext JSX/CommonJS consumers and ESM/CommonJS server rendering passed. These are isolated consumer audit results, not monorepo-wide audit results.

Receipts: `/tmp/cms-ops-{server-tests,studio-tests,server-types,studio-types,build,packed}.log` and `/tmp/cms-ops-production-audit-final.json`. Owned browser/server processes close in fixture cleanup, and the isolated installation is removed after receipt collection. No provider send, ContentFn edit, deployment or push occurred.

## Remaining original scope, classified

- Scheduled publishing is required by SPEC invariant 8. REL-001's optional target time means individual releases may be manual; it does not make scheduler support optional. Current runtime stores `publishAt` but has no due-release executor. Studio states this limitation and exposes no false scheduling control.

- Native Safari, deployment authentication/session/CORS policy and external database/service acceptance remain separate gates. Large-archive streaming/background job integration is not claimed by this bounded synchronous path. Whole-CMS readiness remains incomplete.

## Overview

CmsFn (`cmsfn`) is the **self-hosted authoring studio and content operations layer** for the Superfunctions ecosystem. It provides an editorial UI and workflow system (desk, document editing, media library, preview, review/publish flow, roles/permissions) powered by `contentfn` as the canonical content backend.

CmsFn’s core principle: **all content state lives in `contentfn`**; CmsFn adds:
- schema-aware authoring UI,
- editorial workflows,
- preview/build hooks,
- access control UX and role management integration,
- operational tools (imports, releases, audit logs viewer),
while remaining self-hosted.

**One-sentence goal**: Provide a self-hosted, Sanity-like CMS studio (desk + editor + media + preview + workflows + permissions) built on ContentFn so teams can author and publish content without vendor SaaS.

**Target users**:
- Content editors (non-dev) using a browser-based Studio
- Developers configuring schema, desk structure, and preview integrations
- Operators managing deployments (auth, storage, backups)

**Target environments**:
- Web app (browser) for Studio UI (React-like recommended; Svelte optional)
- Node.js server for Studio backend (auth/session, proxy to contentfn, webhooks/preview endpoints)
- Works behind any reverse proxy; self-hosted.

## Glossary

- **Studio**: The CMS web application used by editors.
- **Desk**: The main navigation/workspace surface (document lists, structure, panes).
- **Pane**: A UI region showing a list, editor, preview, history, etc.
- **Document editor**: Schema-driven form editor for a ContentFn document.
- **Field widget**: A UI component used to edit a field type (string, richtext, reference, asset).
- **Preview**: Live rendering of draft content in a target site/app.
- **Workflow**: Editorial state machine and rules (draft → review → approved → published).
- **Release**: A named batch of changes scheduled for coordinated publish.
- **Role**: A set of permissions for datasets/types/actions.
- **Audit log**: A view over ContentFn events and webhook delivery state.

## Goals

1. CmsFn MUST provide a Sanity-like studio UX: desk navigation, document lists, document editor, and preview.
2. CmsFn MUST be schema-driven, using ContentFn schema to render editors and validate input before write.
3. CmsFn MUST support editorial workflows: drafts, review/approval gates, and publishing/unpublishing.
4. CmsFn MUST provide media (asset) management UX backed by ContentFn assets APIs.
5. CmsFn MUST provide reference selection UX (search/browse) and bounded preview of referenced docs.
6. CmsFn MUST integrate with ContentFn realtime feed for live updates and collaborative preview.
7. CmsFn MUST support role-based access control UX and enforce permissions via server-side authorization.
8. CmsFn MUST support releases (batch publish) and scheduled publishing.
9. CmsFn MUST provide operational tools: import/export triggers, webhook/audit log viewer, dataset selection.
10. CmsFn MUST be self-hosted and must not require external vendor services.

## Non-goals

- CmsFn MUST NOT define its own content storage model; it consumes ContentFn exclusively.
- CmsFn is not a general-purpose page builder; it edits schema-defined documents (richtext + blocks are sufficient).

## Public API

CmsFn exposes both:
- a **Studio web app** (UI surface), and
- an optional **server API** for Studio-specific operations (sessions, role management, preview tokens).

### Canonical envelope + errors

1. CmsFn MUST provide a Sanity-like studio UX: desk navigation, document lists, document editor, and preview.
2. CmsFn MUST be schema-driven, using ContentFn schema to render editors and validate input before write.
3. CmsFn MUST support editorial workflows: drafts, review/approval gates, and publishing/unpublishing.
4. CmsFn MUST provide media (asset) management UX backed by ContentFn assets APIs.
5. CmsFn MUST provide reference selection UX (search/browse) and bounded preview of referenced docs.
6. CmsFn MUST integrate with ContentFn realtime feed for live updates and collaborative preview.
7. CmsFn MUST support role-based access control UX and enforce permissions via server-side authorization.
8. CmsFn MUST support releases (batch publish) and scheduled publishing.
9. CmsFn MUST provide operational tools: import/export triggers, webhook/audit log viewer, dataset selection.
10. CmsFn MUST be self-hosted and must not require external vendor services.

## Non-goals

- CmsFn MUST NOT define its own content storage model; it consumes ContentFn exclusively.
- CmsFn is not a general-purpose page builder; it edits schema-defined documents (richtext + blocks are sufficient).

## Public API

CmsFn exposes both:
- a **Studio web app** (UI surface), and
- an optional **server API** for Studio-specific operations (sessions, role management, preview tokens).

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```

│   └── SPEC.md              # Specification (if exists)
├── packages/                # Shared packages
│   ├── {name}/              # @superfunctions/{name}
│   └── python-{name}/       # Python shared packages
└── _conduct/                # Root artifacts
```

## 🚀 Best Practices

### Super functions ecosystem (Very important)

- Reuse shared packages from `packages/` folder like http abstraction, db abstraction, etc.
- Never duplicate shared code like http adapters, db abstractions, etc.
- Don't reexport http-adapters etc - end consumers of the core function package will use the adapters directly. Refer `authfn` implementation for usage of core http router, core db, http adapters and db interface usage.
- Function packages that accept a `@superfunctions/db` `Adapter` must wrap the incoming adapter internally with their own schema, for example `wrapWithSchema(config.database, getSchema(...))`, before passing it to services/storage. Do not require app consumers to pass `adapterSchema` to `drizzleAdapter`, `kyselyAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or `memoryAdapter`; `adapterSchema` is a deprecated compatibility escape hatch for direct app-level adapter use.

### Code Organization

- Keep shared code in `packages/`
- Keep function-specific code in `{function}/`
- Use TypeScript for type safety
- Provide Python SDKs for backend-focused functions
- Write comprehensive tests

### Documentation

- Update README.md with usage examples
- Create SPEC.md for complex functions
- Document breaking changes
- Keep artifacts in `.conduct/` folders

### Testing

- Use Vitest for TypeScript
- Use pytest for Python
- Maintain high test coverage
- Test adapters separately

### Versioning

- Follow semantic versioning
- Coordinate versions across language SDKs
- Document migration guides for breaking changes

## 🔗 Related Resources

- **Repository**: https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions
- **License**: MIT (most packages) / Apache-2.0 (some packages)
- **Organization**: 21n
- **Contact**: hello@21n.org

## 📝 Notes for AI Agents

1. **Always check both TypeScript and Python** implementations when working on core functions
2. **Respect the naming conventions** - shared packages use `@superfunctions/`, functions use simple names
3. **Create artifacts in `.conduct/` folders**, not in root or arbitrary locations
4. **Avoid nested monorepos** - use subfolders within the main Turbo monorepo
5. **Use Turbo commands** for cross-package operations
6. **Check existing patterns** in similar functions before implementing new features
7. **Maintain consistency** across TypeScript and Python SDKs
8. **Update workspaces** in root `package.json` when adding new packages
9. **Follow existing test patterns** (Vitest for TS, pytest for Python)
10. **Document thoroughly** - this is a developer-focused ecosystem

---

**Package Manager**: npm@10.2.0
**Build Tool**: Turbo v2.0.0

Configure `preview.enabled`, a trusted HTTP(S) `preview.targetOrigin`, and a server-only
`previewSecret` containing at least 32 bytes of unpredictable key material. The optional

choose the signed audience. Draft IDs normalize to their base document IDs.

The preview target imports `verifyPreviewToken` from `@cmsfn/server` and supplies its
own trusted audience plus the dataset and document it is about to read:

```ts
const claims = verifyPreviewToken(secret, token, {
  audience: 'https://preview.example.com', dataset, docId,
});
if (!claims) return new Response('Denied', { status: 403 });

Do not derive the expected audience from untrusted request headers. Verify before reading
any draft. Version 2 tokens intentionally invalidate old unaudienced tokens; upgrade the
CMS issuer and preview target together. Tokens are bearer credentials: the host must
suppress token-bearing URL logs, avoid third-party resources and redirects from its
preview route, and return appropriate no-store/referrer headers. Studio rejects resolver
URLs outside the configured origin or with URL credentials, uses no-referrer iframes,
renews tokens and removes the frame on expiry, denial, timeout or scope change. It cannot
police redirects initiated by the trusted preview target.

For live updates, set `contentfn.realtimeUrl` to the actual HTTP(S)
`/contentfn/events` endpoint. Native EventSource sends browser cookies with credentials;
the host must authenticate those cookies for `realtime.subscribe`. Cross-origin use
requires explicit credentialed CORS and compatible cookie policy. Native EventSource
cannot attach custom bearer headers: use a same-origin authenticated host proxy when the
producer requires headers. Do not put bearer tokens in the events URL. A host-provided
WebSocket URL remains supported but is not the built-in ContentFn HTTP route. Events
must match the active dataset and document before refreshing; closing or changing scope
cancels queued refreshes.

# Studio preview lifecycle and scoped transport

PREVIEW-001 requires actual draft preview, token minting, and ContentFn realtime updates.

foreign origin, a document switch temporarily reused the previous token, and expired
tokens remained visible. `/tmp/cms-preview-baseline.log` records all three failing tests.

The corrected issuer uses trusted configuration for audience and bounded lifetime, signs
version 2 claims with dataset and normalized document scope, and rejects missing or
unavailable authorization. The exported target verifier checks signature, expected
trusted audience, requested dataset/document, and strict expiry. Legacy unaudienced
tokens are intentionally rejected; the issuer and target require coordinated upgrades.

The complete Studio now validates destination origin before minting, bounds token
response reads, disallows token endpoint redirects, renews before expiry, and clears
frames on scope change, denial, failure or timeout. Explicit request deadlines also
handle transports that ignore abort. Expiry is independent of request cancellation.

HTTP(S) realtime configuration uses the real `/contentfn/events` route with browser
cookie credentials. WebSocket configuration remains a host-owned transport option.
Document subscriptions use the actual stored draft ID, because ContentFn routes by exact
ID; token scope uses the base ID. Incoming events must match dataset and document. Native
EventSource cannot attach custom bearer headers; header-authenticated hosts need a
same-origin proxy. Cross-origin deployments require explicit credentialed CORS/cookies.

The installed fixture uses the entire packaged App, real CMS and Content HTTP handlers,
a real token-verifying preview target, and cookie-authorized SSE. It requires a draft
patch to refresh within 2.5 seconds before token renewal could mask a broken subscription.
It also exercises token renewal, scope denial, permission revocation and unsafe resolver
rejection. The fixture uses the shared memory adapter; this browser path does not claim
SQLite or other database persistence evidence.

The preview target remains responsible for avoiding credential-bearing URL logs,
redirects and third-party resource leakage. Native Safari and deployed host/proxy
acceptance remain separate original readiness gates. No Python Studio implementation is
introduced by this browser-specific slice.

Validation results will be recorded after the final source and installed checks.

### Media library

Media pages follow ContentFn's `createdAt` descending, then `assetId` ascending order.
Each page contains at most 50 assets; next/previous navigation replaces the current page.
This is the producer's offset pagination, not a stable snapshot: concurrent uploads or
deletions can shift page boundaries. Refresh returns to the newest page.

`limits.maxUploadBytes` bounds decoded file bytes and is checked against `File.size`
before reading or encoding. Studio defaults to 1 MiB when it is omitted and rejects
invalid nonpositive/noninteger limits. The producer independently enforces its decoded
asset limit and the encoded JSON request limit. Configure the latter for base64 expansion
and metadata; a file passing Studio's check can still exceed a stricter host request
limit. Uploads are not automatically retried after an uncertain network outcome.

File names and MIME metadata are length-bounded; names are rendered as text, never HTML.
Media responses are validated and limited to 2 MiB with a ten-second request deadline.
Access denial removes prior rows. Dataset, endpoint and document changes cancel pending
work and prevent stale selections. Nested object asset fields use literal schema keys,
preserve siblings and reject prototype keys or array traversal. Array-item media editing
is not added by this object-field integration.
EOF
cat > cmsfn/.conduct/media-readiness.md <<'EOF'
# Studio media workflow

MEDIA-001 (P0, original requirements 145–154 / plan phase 08) requires real upload,
deterministic browsing and canonical insertion. Initial regressions reproduced reading
an oversized File before checking its limit, overcounting padded base64, and ignored
disabled asset controls. All three failures are in `/tmp/cms-media-baseline.log`.

The media library checks File.size before reading, validates exact decoded base64 length,
uses bounded metadata transport, replaces deterministic offset pages and clears data on
scope changes or permission revocation. Network requests have explicit deadlines;
unknown provider error strings are not displayed. Filename text cannot become markup.

Nested object asset fields previously omitted media picker options entirely. They now
carry literal schema key segments into immutable insertion, preserving siblings without
splitting dotted keys. Prototype keys and array traversal are rejected. Picker state is
bound to the loaded document and cleared on reload/navigation; stale callbacks cannot
insert into a different document. Array-item media editing remains a separate editor gap.

Producer authorization and byte limits are exercised through actual ContentFn HTTP and
programmatic contracts. The installed full-App fixture configures a persistent test
InMemoryStorageBackend instance and checks uploaded bytes, metadata pages and saved
canonical document references. This proves the browser/transport/producer contract, not
durable filesystem/cloud asset hosting. Offset pagination does not provide snapshot
stability under concurrent insertions/deletions.

Validation receipts will be completed after the final checks. Native Safari and deployed
host acceptance remain separate; no Python Studio implementation is introduced.
EOF","workdir":"/Volumes/Dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/cmsfn-sf-next-readiness","max_output_tokens":500}));

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`

### Adding a Shared Package

2. Package name: `@superfunctions/{name}`
3. Add to workspace (already covered by `packages/*`)

2. Shared/root: `_conduct/{artifact}.md`
3. Use consistent naming: `implementation.md`, `spec.md`, `audit_report.md`, etc.

# Run task across all packages
turbo run build

## 🚀 Best Practices

### Super functions ecosystem (Very important)

- Reuse shared packages from `packages/` folder like http abstraction, db abstraction, etc.
- Never duplicate shared code like http adapters, db abstractions, etc.
- Don't reexport http-adapters etc - end consumers of the core function package will use the adapters directly. Refer `authfn` implementation for usage of core http router, core db, http adapters and db interface usage.
- Function packages that accept a `@superfunctions/db` `Adapter` must wrap the incoming adapter internally with their own schema, for example `wrapWithSchema(config.database, getSchema(...))`, before passing it to services/storage. Do not require app consumers to pass `adapterSchema` to `drizzleAdapter`, `kyselyAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or `memoryAdapter`; `adapterSchema` is a deprecated compatibility escape hatch for direct app-level adapter use.

### Code Organization

- Keep shared code in `packages/`
- Keep function-specific code in `{function}/`
- Use TypeScript for type safety
- Provide Python SDKs for backend-focused functions
- Write comprehensive tests

### Documentation

- Update README.md with usage examples
- Create SPEC.md for complex functions
- Document breaking changes
- Keep artifacts in `.conduct/` folders

### Testing

- Use Vitest for TypeScript
- Use pytest for Python
- Maintain high test coverage
- Test adapters separately

### Versioning

- Follow semantic versioning
- Coordinate versions across language SDKs
- Document migration guides for breaking changes

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── README.md
```

### Examples

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`
- `cachefn/typescript/` + `cachefn/python/`
- `secfn/typescript/` + `secfn/python/`
- `plugfn/core/` + `plugfn/python/`
- `drawfn/core/` (TypeScript only, with React/Svelte adapters)
- `searchfn/` (TypeScript only, browser-focused)

## 🔧 Development Workflow

### Building

```bash
# Build all packages
npm run build

# Build specific package (from root)
turbo run build --filter=authfn
turbo run build --filter=@superfunctions/db

# Build from package directory
cd authfn/ts-sdk && npm run build
```

### Testing

```bash
# Test all packages
npm test

# Test specific package
turbo run test --filter=drawfn

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch
```

### Linting

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Package Manager

- **npm** (v10.2.0+) - Specified in `packageManager` field
- Uses npm workspaces for monorepo management
- Turbo for build orchestration

## 🎯 Key Superfunctions Features

### AuthFn

- Multi-provider authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT)
- Framework-agnostic with adapters for Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- Database-agnostic (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- TypeScript + Python SDKs

### DrawFn

- Cross-framework drawing canvas
- React and Svelte adapters
- Scene management, export capabilities
- Tolerant parsing with version validation

### PlugFn

- Self-hosted integration platform
- 75+ provider integrations (GitHub, Slack, Discord, Linear, Stripe)
- OAuth 2.0 flow handling
- Webhook support
- Multi-tenant with secure token storage

### SearchFn

- Browser-first full-text search
- IndexedDB persistence with in-memory LRU cache
- BM25 scoring
- FlexSearch-compatible API
- Worker-ready with snapshot export/import

### MailFn

- Stable and expiring programmable inboxes
- Cloudflare Email Workers, D1, R2, and Queues deployment adapter
- Raw MIME and attachment evidence, waits, OTP/link extraction, threads, labels, and search
- Typed client, test helpers, CLI, MCP server, custom domains, webhooks, and SendFn composition
- Scoped credentials, retention, audit, quotas, and explicitly gated public-platform controls

### CacheFn

- Multi-tier caching (memory, IndexedDB, external)
- Function memoization
- TTL and invalidation strategies
- Browser and server support

### SecFn

- Secrets vault management
- Access control and permissions
- Rate limiting
- Security monitoring
- Secret scanning

### BotFn

- Multi-platform bot framework
- Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations
- Shared types and persistence layer
- Event-driven architecture

## 🛠️ Common Tasks

### Adding a New Function

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`
4. Create `.conduct/` for artifacts
5. Add to workspace in root `package.json`
6. Package name: `{functionname}` (not scoped unless multi-package)

### Adding a Shared Package

1. Create in `packages/{name}/`
2. Package name: `@superfunctions/{name}`
3. Add to workspace (already covered by `packages/*`)
4. Update dependent packages

### Creating Artifacts

1. Function-specific: `{function}/.conduct/{artifact}.md`
2. Shared/root: `_conduct/{artifact}.md`
3. Use consistent naming: `implementation.md`, `spec.md`, `audit_report.md`, etc.

### Working with Turbo

```bash
# Run task across all packages
turbo run build
turbo run test

# Run for specific package
turbo run build --filter=authfn

# Run with dependencies
turbo run build --filter=authfn...

# Clear cache
turbo run clean
```

## 📚 Important Files

### Root Configuration

- `package.json` - Workspace and script definitions
- `turbo.json` - Turbo build configuration
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript base config (if exists)

### Package Configuration

- `package.json` - Package metadata, dependencies, scripts
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript configuration
- `vitest.config.ts` - Test configuration
- `pyproject.toml` - Python package configuration

### Documentation

- `README.md` - Package overview and usage
- `SPEC.md` - Technical specification (common in larger functions)
- `.conduct/*.md` - Implementation plans, audits, tasks

## 🔍 Finding Code

### Search Patterns

- **Function implementations**: `{function}/typescript/src/` or `{function}/python/{function}/`
- **Tests**: `__tests__/`, `tests/`, `*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`
- **Types**: `types.ts`, `models.py`, `src/types/`
- **Adapters**: `packages/http-*/`, `packages/python-*/`, `adapters/`
- **Examples**: `examples/`, `{function}/examples/`

### Key Directories

```
superfunctions/
├── {function}/              # Core function packages
│   ├── typescript/          # TS implementation
│   ├── python/              # Python implementation
│   ├── .conduct/            # Artifacts
│   ├── README.md            # Documentation
│   └── SPEC.md              # Specification (if exists)
├── packages/                # Shared packages
│   ├── {name}/              # @superfunctions/{name}
│   └── python-{name}/       # Python shared packages
└── _conduct/                # Root artifacts
```

## 🚀 Best Practices

### Super functions ecosystem (Very important)

- Reuse shared packages from `packages/` folder like http abstraction, db abstraction, etc.
- Never duplicate shared code like http adapters, db abstractions, etc.
- Don't reexport http-adapters etc - end consumers of the core function package will use the adapters directly. Refer `authfn` implementation for usage of core http router, core db, http adapters and db interface usage.
- Function packages that accept a `@superfunctions/db` `Adapter` must wrap the incoming adapter internally with their own schema, for example `wrapWithSchema(config.database, getSchema(...))`, before passing it to services/storage. Do not require app consumers to pass `adapterSchema` to `drizzleAdapter`, `kyselyAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or `memoryAdapter`; `adapterSchema` is a deprecated compatibility escape hatch for direct app-level adapter use.

### Code Organization

- Keep shared code in `packages/`
- Keep function-specific code in `{function}/`
- Use TypeScript for type safety
- Provide Python SDKs for backend-focused functions
- Write comprehensive tests

### Documentation

- Update README.md with usage examples
- Create SPEC.md for complex functions
- Document breaking changes
- Keep artifacts in `.conduct/` folders

### Testing

- Use Vitest for TypeScript
- Use pytest for Python
- Maintain high test coverage
- Test adapters separately

### Versioning

- Follow semantic versioning
- Coordinate versions across language SDKs
- Document migration guides for breaking changes

## 🔗 Related Resources

- **Repository**: https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions
- **License**: MIT (most packages) / Apache-2.0 (some packages)
- **Organization**: 21n
- **Contact**: hello@21n.org

## 📝 Notes for AI Agents

1. **Always check both TypeScript and Python** implementations when working on core functions
2. **Respect the naming conventions** - shared packages use `@superfunctions/`, functions use simple names
3. **Create artifacts in `.conduct/` folders**, not in root or arbitrary locations
4. **Avoid nested monorepos** - use subfolders within the main Turbo monorepo
5. **Use Turbo commands** for cross-package operations
6. **Check existing patterns** in similar functions before implementing new features
7. **Maintain consistency** across TypeScript and Python SDKs
8. **Update workspaces** in root `package.json` when adding new packages
9. **Follow existing test patterns** (Vitest for TS, pytest for Python)
10. **Document thoroughly** - this is a developer-focused ecosystem

The media library checks File.size before reading, validates exact decoded base64 length,
uses bounded metadata transport, replaces deterministic offset pages and clears data on
scope changes or permission revocation. Network requests have explicit deadlines;
unknown provider error strings are not displayed. Filename text cannot become markup.

Nested object asset fields previously omitted media picker options entirely. They now
carry literal schema key segments into immutable insertion, preserving siblings without
splitting dotted keys. Prototype keys and array traversal are rejected. Picker state is
bound to the loaded document and cleared on reload/navigation; stale callbacks cannot
insert into a different document. Array-item media editing remains a separate editor gap.

Producer authorization and byte limits are exercised through actual ContentFn HTTP and
programmatic contracts. The installed full-App fixture configures a persistent test
InMemoryStorageBackend instance and checks uploaded bytes, metadata pages and saved
canonical document references. This proves the browser/transport/producer contract, not
durable filesystem/cloud asset hosting. Offset pagination does not provide snapshot
stability under concurrent insertions/deletions.

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat >> cmsfn/studio/README.md <<'EOF'

Reference fields, including fields nested inside objects, use the configured CmsFn API
for candidate discovery. The host must grant `doc.read` for the selected dataset and
every allowed target type. The picker offers a type selector, case-sensitive ID/title/name
filter, refresh and deterministic `_id`-ascending pages of at most 20 published documents.
Each new page replaces the previous page. Selection writes the canonical
`{ _type: 'reference', _ref: id }`; ContentFn remains authoritative when saving, including
when a selected target has since been deleted. Changing document, dataset, type or filter
clears the old candidate scope. Labels are text, truncated to 160 characters.

For a standalone Studio without `cmsfn.apiUrl`, the host may explicitly configure
`references: { authorization: 'contentfn' }`. This delegates candidate authorization to
its ContentFn `query` policy, which must enforce the authenticated subject's dataset and
type access. Without either configuration, candidate discovery denies access. When a
CmsFn URL is present it always takes precedence; UI read flags cannot bypass the server.
Use same-origin authenticated routes or a host proxy; service credentials belong only in
server configuration. Array-item reference editing remains separate editor work.
EOF
cat >> cmsfn/server/README.md <<'EOF'

### Reference candidates

`POST /cmsfn/references/query` accepts `{ dataset, types, search?, cursor?, limit? }`.
The configured dataset and every requested type require `doc.read`. Roles are resolved
once per request; missing, denied or throwing role resolution fails closed before any
upstream query or capability check. `contentfnReferenceHeaders(request)` optionally
supplies trusted ContentFn credentials after authorization; browser headers are not
forwarded automatically. The producer must enforce the configured dataset query contract.

Queries use the published perspective, `_id` ascending and only `_id`, `_type`, `title`
and `name` projection. The response is `{ dataset, data: [{ _id, _type, label }],
nextCursor }`. No document body or arbitrary upstream error detail is returned. Requests
are bounded to 96 KiB, 50 target types, 128-character dataset/type/filter values, 65,536
characters of cursor and 20 candidates. Returned IDs are bounded to 32,768 characters,
labels to 160, and upstream responses to 2 MiB. Oversized pages retry the same cursor
with smaller limits down to one within a ten-second query deadline; an oversized single
candidate fails explicitly. Host identity, credential and capability callbacks retain
 their existing host lifecycle contract.

ContentFn owns keyset cursor validation and dataset isolation. Filter/type/dataset changes
must start a new traversal; this is deterministic pagination, not a snapshot under
concurrent writes. The producer does not include dataset on individual query rows: the
CMS response binds it to the authorized query and rejects a conflicting dataset if one
is supplied by the upstream. HTML/empty HTTP 401/403 responses are treated as denial.
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('cmsfn/server/README.md');p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('\n their existing', '\ntheir existing'))
PY

# Producer richtext block limits

previously validated portable block/span keys and mark allow lists but imposed no block
count, allowing direct writes to bypass Studio prechecks. `limits.maxRichtextBlocks` now
resolves to 5,000 by default and accepts a positive safe integer override. Status exposes
that resolved value. Schema-driven validation applies it to nested objects and array
alternatives on create, patch, fork, restore, manual publication and scheduled publication.
Read normalization remains uncapped so existing content can be inspected and corrected.

Import uses a separate limit-only traversal before mutation. Archive revision records
carry snapshots but no historical schemas, so only richtext declarations in the archive's
latest schema can be classified. Unknown/removed historical fields and arbitrary JSON
remain compatible; this is not a global richtext/archive-array cap. Later restore and
publication always validate against the current schema and configured limit. Import
transaction recursion preserves the configured override. No existing document or snapshot

# Producer richtext block limits

previously validated portable block/span keys and mark allow lists but imposed no block
count, allowing direct writes to bypass Studio prechecks. `limits.maxRichtextBlocks` now
resolves to 5,000 by default and accepts a positive safe integer override. Status exposes
that resolved value. Schema-driven validation applies it to nested objects and array
alternatives on create, patch, fork, restore, manual publication and scheduled publication.
Read normalization remains uncapped so existing content can be inspected and corrected.

Import uses a separate limit-only traversal before mutation. Archive revision records
carry snapshots but no historical schemas, so only richtext declarations in the archive's
latest schema can be classified. Unknown/removed historical fields and arbitrary JSON
remain compatible; this is not a global richtext/archive-array cap. Later restore and
publication always validate against the current schema and configured limit. Import
transaction recursion preserves the configured override. No existing document or snapshot
is truncated. Failed content writes do not append revision/event/audit records.

  restore/scheduled publication. Revision/event/audit counts and existing content remain
